findings.text: non-blocking: `_ledger_run_rows` swallows any ledger failure into `None`, and `_section_run_unlanded` then returns False at :3442 when no live pointer exists, so a promoted run whose pointer promotion has already removed (reckon/crew/promotion.py:195) releases its waiters when the ledger cannot be read — a fail-open in the guard this node adds, where `_request_state` at :3512 returns PENDING on the same unreadable evidence.

non-blocking: `_section_run_unlanded` re-derives the (plan, section) identity over ledger rows, scans `ledger.load(project)` for `promoted_revision` and applies `_revision_is_ancestor` itself, duplicating the derivation reckon/crew/runs.py:2348 `_unloaded_sections` already owns without calling or extending it, and uses `normalize_section` ("§40") where that owner uses `_plan_html.section_record_id` ("s40"), so the two answers about a section's landed state can drift.

non-blocking: `_promote` writes the ledger row but leaves the upstream's live pointer in place, so the promotion case holds through `_manifest_status` at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3453 and never through the ledger branch at :3415; deleting `_ledger_run_rows` outright leaves all four tests green, while the production promotion release (reckon/crew/promotion.py:195 removes the pointer first) depends on exactly that branch.

non-blocking: `commits:` lists three of the five reviewed commits; f0608177 and 8e989cbf (the reviewed head) are absent, so a coordinator reading the record alone cannot see the no-checkout hold or the discarded-promoted-run fix.

non-blocking: `after_suite` records revision bf3ff50d and a command without `-n 4`, while the log it cites (logs/armed-after_suite.log) has twenty-two lines of header naming revision 8e989cbf and command `-q -n 4`; the arm ran at the reviewed head, so the recorded revision and command are stale rather than the measurement.

non-blocking: the reproduction log names `test_a_delivered_unlanded_run_holds_the_wait_until_armed_into_head`, which does not exist in the landed file (it is `..._until_merged_into_head` at tests/test_a_wait_releases_when_its_upstream_lands.py:256), so its failing ids cannot be mapped to the landed tests.
